blocking_findings.classification: SHOWN source, actual fixture identities and pure synthetic reproduction
blocking_findings.title: loaded overwrites counting socket guards, so swallowed socket attempts can evade teardown
blocking_findings.detail: The autouse no_native fixture installs socket connect/connect_ex/getaddrinfo closures that append to attempted. The explicit loaded fixture subsequently replaces all three with tests.test_companion_probe_policy.forbidden, which raises but has no counter. Runtime hook inspection after fixture setup observed these non-counting replacements in all three cases. HTTP/process counting guards remain active.
blocking_findings.reproduction: A purely synthetic AST-compiled fixture on SimpleNamespace objects emulated the observed loaded replacement. The replacement guard raised and its exception was deliberately swallowed; attempted remained [] and the post-yield assertion did not fail. Equivalent swallowed HTTP/process guard errors did make teardown fail.
blocking_findings.impact: This is not an actual outbound request or a claim that the three normal cases made socket attempts. It is a hole in the requested counter proof: zero counted attempts does not establish zero swallowed socket attempts. The checkpoint's 'counts every forbidden attempt' statement remains unsupported.
blocking_findings.required_disposition: Keep counting guards effective after loaded setup, or share accounting with the replacement guards, and demonstrate the composed fixture catches a swallowed socket-guard error using synthetic objects only. No fix implemented here.
blocking_findings.scope_of_rejection: Full harness-counter correction only; the pre-existing diagnosis/recommendation is not invalidated.
